findings.evidence: Lines 76, 86, and 95 expose the three bodies; grep finds `toPerm_ofPerm` and operation lemmas but no `TimePerm.ext` or `toPerm_injective`.
findings.fix: Remove these `@[expose]` annotations and add an `@[ext]` theorem (or `toPerm_injective`) establishing equality from equality of underlying permutations; keep the existing constructor/projection simp lemmas as the opaque API.
findings.issue: `TimePerm`, `toPerm`, and `ofPerm` are all `@[expose]`, and no `TimePerm.ext` or injectivity theorem characterizes equality through `toPerm`; downstream equality proofs therefore depend on unfolding the synonym.

findings.evidence: Line 94 has `@[expose] def finitary`; lines 103–106 immediately provide the `[simp]` membership characterization.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from `finitary`; define `mem_finitary` with an opaque-safe proof such as `:= (Iff.rfl)` if needed.
findings.issue: `Equiv.Perm.finitary` exposes its structure body even though `mem_finitary` already provides its characteristic membership API.

summary: The new action types expose implementation bodies while lacking the extensionality API needed to use them opaquely.
